FED BALANCE SHEET / NET LIQUIDITY — QT ended, slow drain via liabilities. QT was formally ended in December 2025 (Fed now reinvesting principal to hold nominal size roughly constant). H.4.1 (6/3/26): total assets $6,711bn (Treasuries $4,469bn, MBS $1,965bn); reserve balances $3,014bn; TGA $846bn; RRP/ON RRP $326bn. Net liquidity ~$5,830bn vs ~$6,070bn a year ago; reserves down from ~$3,294bn YoY. So even post-QT, liabilities (TGA rebuild) are quietly draining reserves.

FUNDING PLUMBING — FIRST SIGNS OF STRESS (the key new wrinkle). SOFR ~3.62% (6/6/26). More recent commentary flags SRF usage back around ~$100bn and overnight repo trading ABOVE the SRF rate "in the past few days," with the Fed adding earlier-in-day SRF operations to keep control of SOFR. This is reserve scarcity emerging, not a crisis — but it is the first plumbing tell.

MATURITY WALL — largely defused for 2026-27. Most 2026-27 HY/loan maturities pushed out via extensions/repricings; >$700bn of bonds now due 2027-29 (>$350bn in 2029). US loans: 67% 'B', 14% 'CCC+ or below'. Refinancing demand for 'B-' and lower has SOFTENED as capital rotates to higher quality — the one place small/low-quality refi stress is visible.
